title: Wharness Session Attempt Ledger v1
description: The measured state of one Main Request, carried on every correction wave as attempts/state.json. Rounds are Wharnex's own measurement of what actually happened on this machine, not planner claims: a round that failed must reach the next request whether or not the planner recorded it. The planner's cumulative prose ledger travels beside this file as attempts/ledger.md.

root_request_id.description: The Main Request this ledger belongs to. A ledger is never served to a different Main Request: it records what worked and failed while pursuing one goal.

round.description: One-based position of the request being prepared, counting every measured round plus this one.

max_rounds.description: The effort level's automated attempt ceiling. Zero means no fixed numeric limit.

narrative_request_id.description: Which round authored the ledger currently in force. A round that returned none is visible here rather than silently presenting stale prose as current.

kind.description: The request lineage kind that produced this round.

outcome.description: Wharnex's closed-set classification. policy_blocked means the plan never executed and the patch may be sound; verification_failed means it ran and was wrong. Collapsing the two would send the next round rewriting correct source.

detail.description: The single most actionable sentence about this round, already truncated. Full diagnostics stay in the request message and the event log.

commands.description: argv lines that actually ran, with their exit codes, so a later round can see a tool was already tried and how it ended.
